title: How PNG Works: Compromising Speed for Quality
beats: JPEG artifacts on text vs lossless PNG; promises QOI, a 50x faster format, at the end
You are asked to compress an RGB image to fewest bits, must be exactly reversible
Exploit redundancy via Huffman on a single channel, 4-value toy image; tree built by merging least frequent
1.89 vs 2 bits is misleading since the tree must be stored; PNG uses Huffman but later
Huffman ignores neighbours; run-length encoding for repeats, then an image where it fails
LZSS back references: text example, sliding window and lookahead defined
Step through the encoding char by char: literal, (offset,len) pairs, window slides
Decode the stream to show nothing is lost
Window size changes results; real values 32KB/258B; overlap matches (len>offset); min length 3
Overlap trick yields run-length encoding for free
Gradient image breaks both LZSS and Huffman: 'so depressing'
Transform the problem instead of inventing a new method: filtering turns gradient into constant differences
Five PNG filters (none, sub, up, average, Paeth), mod 256 wraparound with 134-139=251
Brute-force filter choice is 5^240; heuristic min sum of abs differences instead
No proof this heuristic is best; nobody has beaten it
Full pipeline: filter, LZSS, Huffman = deflate
PNG is complicated and slow; sets up QOI
QOI: five byte-aligned rules (run, small diff, big diff, index of seen, raw) on 64-pixel toy image
50 bytes vs 192; 20-50x faster; one-page spec vs PNG monster; exercise to implement
Moral: simple solutions deserve respect; manage complexity

theory: The video builds a stack of tools by having each one visibly fail on a tiny input, so every new component is the answer to a failure the learner just saw. Honest caveats (misleading 1.89 bits, no proof for the heuristic) buy trust for the dense later material.
velocity: Scene builder: for multi-stage pipelines generate a 'counterexample input' scene per stage that breaks the previous stage before introducing the next
Orchestrator: when playbook is 'stack of tools', insert a failure beat before each new tool and a callback in the final recap
Evals: check that every named technique is preceded by a shown failure or need within ~60 s
quote: we just spent all this time going through our two main weapons
